title: Error occurs when using converters.optional and converters.pipe together
description: In 24.x, defining a field with converter=attrs.converters.optional(attrs.converters.pipe(str, int)) errors at construction, while 23.2.0 worked and converted '1' to 1.
acceptance_rules: A field with converter=optional(pipe(str, int)) and default=None constructs without error
Constructing the class with a string converts it through the pipe to int

title: Upgrade to 24.1.0 seems to break assignment to fields with chained converters
description: Fields declared with a list of converters (converter=[foo, bar]) raise AttributeError on assignment after 24.1.0; chained converters must all run.
acceptance_rules: Assigning to a field with converter=[foo, bar] applies every converter in order
Assignment to such a field does not raise AttributeError

title: attr.filters.exclude or include not simultaneously usable with validators.in_ set
description: Calling attrs.asdict/as_tuple with an exclude/include filter on frozen nodes whose attributes carry validators.in_ raises TypeError: unhashable type.
acceptance_rules: attrs.asdict with an exclude or include filter works on frozen classes
Filtering does not raise TypeError when attributes use validators.in_

title: kw_only with default breaks __attrs_pre_init__ call
description: Defining a kw_only field with a default raises SyntaxError during @define; the class should be constructible and __attrs_pre_init__ should be called.
acceptance_rules: A kw_only field with a default does not raise SyntaxError at class definition
The class constructs successfully and __attrs_pre_init__ runs

title: AttributeError propagation is broken in cached_property with slots=True
description: On a slots=True attrs class, an AttributeError raised inside a property is swallowed and reported as a missing attribute instead of propagating.
acceptance_rules: An AttributeError raised inside a property propagates unchanged on slots=True classes
Accessing a cached_property that raises AttributeError surfaces that original error

title: Test failure with Python 3.13: TestUpdateAbstractMethods.test_remain_abstract[False] does not raise the expected TypeError
description: An attrs class inheriting from abc.ABC without implementing abstract methods should remain abstract and raise TypeError on instantiation; the non-slots case regressed.
acceptance_rules: An attrs class that inherits an abstract class but omits abstract methods remains abstract
Instantiating such a class raises TypeError

title: Compatibility with Python 3.11
description: Some attrs tests fail under Python 3.11 (e.g. test_init_subclass_vanilla); super().__init_subclass__ must work for non-attrs subclasses.
acceptance_rules: super().__init_subclass__ works when the subclass is not an attrs class
attrs classes are compatible with Python 3.11

title: attr._cmp stub uses undefined name
description: The attr/_cmp.pyi stub imports the name _CompareWithType which does not exist anywhere else in the repo; the stub must only reference defined names.
acceptance_rules: src/attr/_cmp.pyi references only names that are defined in the repo
The stub is type-checkable

title: threading.local global variable in _make.py breaks (cloud)pickling
description: A module-level threading.local (e.g. _already_repring) in _make.py prevents attrs-based objects from being pickled by cloudpickle.
acceptance_rules: attrs-based objects can be pickled with cloudpickle
The module has no unpicklable threading.local in the generated-class path

title: Frozen Exceptions cannot be thrown from Exception Handler in PyPy
description: A frozen, slots, auto_exc attrs exception class cannot be raised from an exception handler using 'raise ... from None' on PyPy, unlike CPython.
acceptance_rules: A frozen auto_exc attrs exception class can be raised from an exception handler with from None
The exception is raised identically on CPython and PyPy

title: Inherited attributes of subclasses no longer compare equal to the equivalent attributes of base class
description: Since 20.1.0, attr.fields(SubClass)[0] != attr.fields(BaseClass)[0] for an inherited attribute, though their names are equal; inherited attributes must compare equal.
acceptance_rules: Inherited attributes compare equal to the base class's equivalent attributes
attr.fields(BaseClass)[0] == attr.fields(SubClass)[0] for an inherited attribute

title: Using slots class overrides custom __setattr__ in 20.1.0
description: A custom __setattr__ defined on a slots=True attrs class is replaced by the default slot wrapper since 20.1.0; the custom method must be preserved.
acceptance_rules: A custom __setattr__ on a slots=True attrs class is preserved
Assigning a field on such a class invokes the user-defined __setattr__

title: Hybrid behavior doesn't work when maybe_cls=None and no annotations
description: @attr.define with a plain attr.field() and no type annotations does not follow the documented auto_attribs detection heuristic and errors.
acceptance_rules: @attr.define with a plain attr.field() and no annotations follows the documented auto_attribs heuristic
Defining such a class does not raise an unhandled error

title: @attr.define fails to auto-detect __eq__
description: @attr.define overrides a user-defined __eq__ unless eq=False; it should auto-detect a user __eq__ and not replace it.
acceptance_rules: @attr.define auto-detects a user-defined __eq__ and does not override it
A user __eq__ that raises ValueError is invoked when comparing

title: Restore __setattr__ when subclassing and we didn't write a new __setattr__
description: Subclassing a frozen attrs class makes the subclass frozen too because __setattr__ is not restored; a non-frozen subclass must get object.__setattr__ back.
acceptance_rules: A non-frozen subclass of a frozen attrs class is not itself frozen
The subclass restores __setattr__ to object.__setattr__ unless overridden

title: attr.asdict(retain_collection_types=False) doesn't support frozenset
description: attr.asdict with retain_collection_types=False converts set to list but leaves frozenset as frozenset; frozenset should also convert to a list.
acceptance_rules: attr.asdict(retain_collection_types=False) converts frozenset to list
attr.asdict converts set to list

title: Python 3.10 compatibility
description: Under Python 3.10, PEP 563 string annotations break assertions about types derived from variable annotations (PEP 526); attrs must handle stringified annotations.
acceptance_rules: attrs works with PEP 563 string annotations (from __future__ import annotations)
Classes using variable annotations construct correctly under stringified annotations

title: Using field transformer breaks integration with hypothesis
description: Attributes transformed by a field_transformer (Callable[[type, list[Attribute]], list[Attribute]]) are not cast to the generated class by hypothesis, breaking integration.
acceptance_rules: Attributes transformed by a field_transformer are recognized by hypothesis
Hypothesis-generated values are cast to the generated attrs class

title: Missing type annotations for attrs.cmp_using
description: attrs.cmp_using is not declared in attrs/__init__.pyi, so mypy reports 'Module has no attribute cmp_using' even though it runs fine.
acceptance_rules: attrs.cmp_using is declared in attrs/__init__.pyi
A mypy check that uses attrs.cmp_using reports no missing-attribute error

title: Typing error when defining an enum of an attrs class
description: An Enum of an @attrs.define class gives mypy errors (though it works at runtime); an Enum of an @attrs.frozen class errors at runtime.
acceptance_rules: An Enum of an @attrs.define class is accepted by mypy
An Enum of an @attrs.frozen class works at runtime

title: TypeError when calling super() in decorated method
description: Calling super().f() inside a decorated method on an attrs subclass raises 'TypeError: super(type, obj): obj must be an instance or subtype of type'.
acceptance_rules: Calling super().method() inside a decorated method on an attrs subclass works
No TypeError: super(type, obj) is raised
